trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied MCP tool argument filePath may be read from the local filesystem by context_import; at the pinned commit nothing decides it: the path goes straight to fs.readFileSync, and the parse/read error text is returned verbatim to the caller (CWE-209 content/existence oracle).

landing_point.why: The summary names context_import and filePath; the only use of filePath there is the unvalidated fs.readFileSync, and the error echo is a few lines below.

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool call context_import (error branch echoes error.message)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only candidate neighbour is the existence check in context_set_project_dir (src/index.ts:501-506). A solver could dismiss it as a directory existence probe for a separate feature, not a file read.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Importing a file that context_export just wrote must keep working. Export writes to os.tmpdir()/memory-keeper-export-<id>.json, and the existing tests import from temp dirs. An allow-list that is too tight, or the deny-list validator's existsSync/system-dir rules, could break round-trip import.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: context_set_project_dir echoes 'Directory not found: <path>' after fs.existsSync on a caller-supplied path, which reveals whether a local path exists
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Existence-only, a different feature (git project dir), and no file content is read
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 1200 lines from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An import-time option that reads each fileCache entry's file_path from disk to refresh content (a 'rehydrate cache' mode)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file cache stores real paths, and a maintainer could plausibly re-read them on import to refresh stale content. That would put a second read of attacker-chosen paths behind the import file, a HOW-type route the filePath check never covers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Accept a caller-supplied configPath for profile loading, which reads and parses a JSON file and warns with error.message
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: loadConfigFile already takes a path parameter, so exposing it through a tool or an env override is a small, natural extension. It would be a second JSON-file reader in another module.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Wire the existing deny-list validateFilePath into import as the 'fix', which still allows ~/.ssh, home dotfiles and absolute paths outside /etc,/sys,/proc
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper already exists and is tested but is unused in the handler, so a maintainer reaching for it is realistic. It is a tempting but ineffective defence.

O9_family: path traversal / arbitrary local file read, with error-message information disclosure (CWE-22, CWE-209)

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=20, tsc, jest 30, better-sqlite3 native addon (package.json:10,13,54,61,78,83)

j.j_sites_touched: src/index.ts (per candidate metadata c_site_files=1; diff empty)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Call the existing deny-list validateFilePath(filePath,'read') before readFileSync. It blocks /etc,/sys,/proc and '..', but home-directory secrets and other absolute paths stay readable, and the error echo still leaks.

out_of_scope_notes: context_import inserts caller-controlled file_path/content into file_cache without validation (src/index.ts:1771-1786); this is data integrity, not a read.
Many handlers echo raw error.message (e.g. src/index.ts:1486, 1902); this is general CWE-209 outside this advisory's sink.
